key_insight: Instead of following a pre-committed pipeline schedule, make scheduling decisions at runtime based on which tasks are actually ready; this readiness-driven approach reduces idle bubbles and stage misalignment under variable computation/communication.
problem_solved: Pipeline-parallel training suffers when real task readiness diverges from static or profiled schedules—causing stages to wait for unavailable work, creating idle bubbles, misalignment, and lowered hardware utilization and throughput.
method: Continuously monitor task readiness (compute/communication completion signals) and permit dynamic reordering of pipeline tasks rather than following a fixed pre-committed schedule.
Make lightweight, low-latency scheduling decisions that opportunistically execute any ready work to fill bubbles and re-align stages, maintaining pipeline flow under runtime variability.
Integrate with pipeline-parallel runtimes without heavy profiling or offline schedule generation, keeping overhead low while improving robustness to heterogeneity and transient delays.
impact: Practitioners get higher and more stable training throughput on heterogeneous or variable clusters, reducing end-to-end training time and making pipeline parallelism more practical in real-world, non-deterministic environments.

paper_title: A Readiness-Driven Runtime for Pipeline-Parallel Training under Runtime Variability
paper_authors: Ruitao Liu, Xinyang Tian, Shuo Chen, Tingrui Zhang, Guang Yang
